text:
A: Hi. Can you hear me?
B: Yeah, er, yeah. Hi. I'm Craig.
A: Aneesa. I'm in Bradford.
B: Lowestoft. Suffolk.
A: Is that the one right on the coast?
B: Yeah. Most easterly bit of the country, so. That's what it's known for really.
A: Oh, I didn't know that. Do you live near the sea?
B: Sort of, yeah. Ten minute walk. I take the dog along the front early, when it's quiet. Gets windy, mind.
A: That sounds nice, actually. What kind of dog?
B: Staffy. Dexter. He's a bit chunky.
A: We don't have a dog. My brother keeps asking but my mum says no. He's seventeen, he'd never walk it.
B: Ha. No, probably not. It's sort of mostly me with Dexter. My wife works shifts.
A: What do you do?
B: Er... nothing at the minute. I was a welder. Offshore yard. Got laid off, then the back went. So I'm looking for something lighter.
A: Sorry, that sounds difficult.
B: Yeah. It's alright. It is what it is. You?
A: I'm doing a psychology degree, part-time, with the Open University. And I work in a fragrance shop on Saturdays.
B: Oh right. Psychology. So you're like, working out what this is all about, then? The study?
A: Ha, a bit. I can't help it. I think the photo ratings are the main thing, first impressions, and then these calls test whether you change your mind. And the surveys after, obviously.
B: Right. I just put whatever, to be honest.
A: That's fine. That's probably more useful to them than me overthinking it.
B: Ha. Yeah.
A: Is welding hard to learn? I've always wondered. It looks very precise.
B: Erm, it's practice really. MIG's easier, stick takes longer to get right. You've got to keep a steady hand and watch your pool, the molten bit. Get the speed wrong and it's all lumpy. I watch loads of videos of people doing it still, rebuilding old trailers and that. Saw one last week, bloke took this trailer that was basically rust and cut it all back, new box section, welded it up lovely. I could watch that all day.
A: I get that. I draw geometric patterns, ink. It's the same sort of thing, I think, steady hand, and if one line's off the whole thing's off.
B: Yeah, that's it. Is that the one behind you?
A: Yeah.
B: That's tidy, that.
A: Thank you. Do you still do any welding? Just for yourself?
B: Not really. I've got a motorbike in the yard, a 125, I'm meant to be doing it up. Been two years.
A: Two years? What's stopping you?
B: Dunno. I just go out and look at it. Bloke I had on earlier, Mark, he's got a car in his garage the same. He said we should start a club.
A: Ha. You'd need a planner. I'd make you one, colour-coded.
B: Ha. Yeah, Gemma'd love that. Yeah, it's alright, actually. Might do a bit this weekend.
